headline: Bruins’ Marat Khusnutdinov signs 3-year, $3.95-million extension: Why the timing was right
take:
The Athletic reports that the Bruins have signed Marat Khusnutdinov to a three-year, $3.95-million extension, with the 24-year-old currently in the second season of a two-year, $1.85 million deal. He was drafted 37th overall by the Wild in 2020 out of SKA St. Petersburg 2.

Our numbers say the Bruins are paying for solid depth play, not a breakout. So far this season Khusnutdinov has three goals and three assists in 12 games, but he has scored about one goal more than the quality of his chances would predict (3 goals on 2.02 expected goals, a measure of how good his shots were), so some of that scoring may cool off. The underlying play is steadier: BOS controls 54.64% of the expected goals when he is on the ice at 5-on-5, though the team does slightly better overall with him off it (down 0.92 percentage points). Our model projects just 0.71 expected goals per 60 minutes, which fits a 13.93-minute-a-night role. That role matters for Boston, who sit at 9-2-1 and have been carried by goaltending, with 11.1 goals saved above expected. A cheap, locked-in forward who holds his own at even strength helps a team that needs its depth to keep tilting the ice.
